leverage.exposure: No leveraged position is open right now and the balance is positive. Both recommendations would open one briefly, and the sequencing — not the price — is the real risk. Each buy resolves before its funding sale can be made, so the balance goes negative between winning an auction and selling the paired player, and a negative balance at the matchday lock scores zero for the entire matchday. The saving grace is timing: both auctions resolve several days before the lock, and the sale-to-Kickbase instrument settles instantly at market value, so the exposure is minutes of execution rather than days of drift. But it is entirely execution-dependent: if Georg wins either auction and does not make the paired sale, the position stays leveraged, and the keeper leg is the more dangerous of the two because the sale cannot even be prepared in advance without leaving the squad without a goalkeeper. Both caps were set so that the finish is non-negative in every branch, including both auctions landing.

binding_gap: The binding constraint is not headcount and not the spending floor — it is that the eleven contains a confirmed absentee who will score nothing, with no bench to replace him and no room to simply add a twelfth body. So the gap is quality in one occupied slot, and the fix is a paired buy-and-sell rather than a purchase. Midfield is where the hole sits; it is filled by buying a defender and moving to a five-at-the-back shape, which is legal and which trades a zero for the highest defensive mean available. The secondary gap is the keeper slot, occupied by the squad's only falling asset and its lowest-scoring fit starter.

verdict.detail: Two paired trades are on the table and both are slot swaps, not squad additions — that is what makes them affordable. Priority one is to RAISE the standing Pinckert bid to the affordability ceiling: he is still listed, ours is still the only offer, and the auction resolves tomorrow afternoon. He was re-verified this run as a fit, dated, confirmed starter with full participation in both matchdays, and he replaces a midfielder who is confirmed out injured. The near-identical Rohr precedent — same market-value band, lost twice by underbidding — is the reason not to sit on the current number. Priority two is new and unusual: the first goalkeeper buy this ledger has ever recommended, because the man sold to fund it is the dearer and lower-scoring of the two keepers, so the swap adds points and frees cash at once. Both buys are capped so the balance finishes non-negative even if both land. Nothing else on the board clears its cost.

sell.reason: One sale is a live conditional leg already on the books: the midfielder confirmed out with acute back trouble, who is currently occupying a place in the fielded eleven while contributing nothing. He must only be sold once the defender purchase actually lands — if that auction is lost the sale must not happen and the squad stays as it is. The new sale added this run is the incumbent goalkeeper, and the ground is explicitly not fitness: he is fit, played both matchdays, and his club has only one absentee. He is sold because he is the worse and the dearer of two keepers competing for the single keeper slot, and because he is the only holding in the squad whose market value is falling — every other asset is rising. That sale is likewise conditional and must follow the keeper purchase, never precede it, because a squad with no goalkeeper enters no legal formation.
